clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old man presented with a 20-day progressive illness beginning with acute onset nausea, vomiting, and dizziness after lunch. Fever (maximum 39°C) developed 15 days into the course. Physical examination revealed meningeal signs (neck stiffness) and sluggish light reflex. CSF analysis showed pleocytosis (210 × 10^9/L) with lymphocytic predominance (72% lymphocytes, 16% neutrophils), markedly elevated protein (1371.5 mg/dL), and low glucose (1.1 mmol/L). NGS identified Listeria monocytogenes with 95.63% relative abundance. Blood culture confirmed Listeria infection with elevated WBC (19.52 × 10^9/L). Brain MRI demonstrated lesions in the right pontine and brachium pontis consistent with encephalitis. Initial treatment with acyclovir and dexamethasone was ineffective. Ampicillin 2g IV q4h was initiated on the third day of admission. After 50 days of hospitalization, the patient's consciousness returned to normal with normalization of blood routine, indicating successful treatment response.
